thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-rate CUDA OOMs observed on decode pool (us-west-2). Route: /v1/stream (decoder). Spike start ~2248887700. Pager notified.

maya: got it, joining. @sre_oncall are you seeing this too?

sre_oncall: I'm on. grabbing logs now. initial read: lots of long-lived streams with huge token growth, and CUDA OOM traces on gke-decode-3. possible runaway generation.

ben: kube events show decode-runtime pods restarting: CrashLoopBackOff -> OOMKilled repeatedly. node GPU memory pressure causing node flaps.

alex: pasted logs:
```
E CUDA: out of memory while allocating 3.2 GiB
E decode: kv_cache allocation failed
W runtime: falling back to software pager
```

eng-runtime: metrics: avg tokens per stream +3x on this route, concurrent streams spiked ~6x. streaming sessions are long-lived so batching not triggering.

maya: can we short-circuit by limiting max_tokens at the edge or drop sessions that look abusive? want to avoid large-scale scale-up.

sre_oncall: immediate mitigation: enforce request cap on /v1/stream to max_tokens=1024 and throttle concurrency to 50 per node via rate-limiter. applying now.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: throttle-config v5 -> production (canary first). Diff:
```
- streaming.max_tokens: 8192
+ streaming.max_tokens: 1024 (temporary)
+ throttle.concurrent_per_node: 50
```

ops-bot: canary rollout succeeded on decode-1..3, proceeding to remaining nodes.

ben: after throttle rollout, OOMs down but still a few CUDA bursts on older inflight sessions that exceeded memory before cap took effect.

customer-success: receiving customer reports: app-plugins-prod seeing dropped streams / 5xx, 3 tickets so far.

maya: quick estimate from logs: ~0.8% of streaming requests returned 5xx during a ~3 minute spike window (2248887700-2248887940). prepping customer note.

eng-runtime: discovered old behavior: legacy clients can set max_tokens via a request header which bypassed API validation. will patch to validate that header.

alex: preparing patch to reject header max_tokens > 5000. testing now.

sre_oncall: also enabling overflow fallback to a lower-memory quantized model for this route (small-decode-quant) to avoid hard OOMs at cost of quality. rolling out.

deploy-bot: fallback policy rollout in progress.

ben: temporarily added +2 GPU nodes to absorb load while throttles and fallbacks stabilize.

maya: logging: please append incident doc https://internal.redwood/incidents/2248887776 and preserve logs.

alex: header validation merged and deployed. monitoring closely.

eng-runtime: combined mitigations (throttle + header validation + fallback + temporary scale) have dropped CUDA OOMs to near zero. 5xx rate back to baseline.

customer-success: drafting proactive outreach to impacted customers. estimated window 3 minutes. impacted: app-plugins-prod (high), analytics-saas (medium). cc @maya for wording.

maya: draft will include apology, short root cause (runaway generation + header bypass), what we did (throttle, header validation, fallback, scale-up), status (mitigated), next steps (postmortem ETA).

sre_oncall: ops checklist:
- confirm nodes stable
- capture 30m of heap/GPU metrics post-incident
- preserve logs for 72h
- add alert for header-based max_tokens bypass

ben: nodes stable, no OOMs in last 6 minutes. uploaded nvidia-smi and dmesg snapshots to incident doc.

eng-runtime: follow-ups:
- alex: API change to ignore header max_tokens entirely (PR #4521) -> in progress
- rita: add per-session KV cache soft-limits (ticket INF-212)
- maya: write postmortem and schedule blameless review

incident-bot: SCHEDULED: oncall handoff to night shift @sre_night at 2248888800. please verify runbook.

sre_oncall: handing off. status: mitigated, monitoring. handoff notes in incident doc. no active outages, some requests routed to quantized fallback (reduced quality).

maya: starting postmortem doc with timeline, telemetry, customer impact, and action items. tagging @customer-success for message review.

customer-success: outreach assigned to casey. will coordinate.

eng-runtime: perf follow-up to prevent KV cache bloat on long streams. ETA ~2 weeks.

sre_oncall: closing pager. reopen if anything flares. :thumbsup:

maya: postmortem draft link: https://internal.redwood/postmortems/2248887776-draft

incident-bot: RESOLVED: mitigations applied, monitoring healthy. recorded metadata: root_cause=header_max_tokens_bypass + runaway_generation; impact=~0.8% 5xx for ~3 minutes; mitigations=throttle, header validation, model fallback, temporary node scale-up.

sre_oncall: moving action items to ops board. handoff complete.
